blocks.text: Fraser Valley Condos Just Dropped Under the Zero-PTT Line (2026)

parts.t: The benchmark Fraser Valley condo is
as of August 2026. A year ago it was about $512,000. That 8.9% drop moved the typical condo under a line most first-time buyers have never heard of:
, the price at which BC's first-time buyer exemption wipes out Property Transfer Tax completely.

I've sold in the Fraser Valley for 11+ years. This is the first time since 2021 that the average condo sits under that line. Here's what it means in dollars, what happens above it, and why the timing matters.

blocks.text: The three PTT tiers for first-time buyers

parts.t: Property Transfer Tax in BC is 1% on the first $200,000 and 2% on everything from $200,000 to $2 million. On a $466,100 condo that's
due at closing. The first-time buyer program changes that based on price:

To qualify you need to be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, have lived in BC for the last 12 months (or filed two BC tax returns in the last six years), never have owned a principal residence anywhere in the world, and move in within 92 days.

blocks.text: The math on a benchmark condo

parts.t: Notice the townhome saves the same $8,000 whether it's $520,000 or $835,000. The exemption doesn't get bigger as the price climbs; it just stops at $860,000. If you're shopping near that ceiling, a $20,000 difference in price can be an $8,000 difference in tax.

blocks.text: If you buy new, the numbers get much bigger

parts.t: This is the part almost nobody is talking about. Two separate programs apply to new construction and presales:
Full PTT exemption on new homes up to
, for any buyer, not just first-timers. On a $750,000 new townhome, that's $13,000 gone.
Federal First-Time Home Buyers' GST Rebate.
Signed into law March 12, 2026. First-time buyers get
on a new home up to $1,000,000 (max $50,000), phasing out to zero at $1.5 million. Applies to any builder agreement signed on or after March 20, 2025. Presales qualify.
Stack them on a $750,000 new townhome: $13,000 PTT waived plus $37,500 GST rebate =

The federal rebate uses a different first-time buyer test than BC: you qualify if you haven't owned and lived in a home in the current year or the previous four calendar years. So some buyers who've owned before still qualify for the GST rebate even though they don't qualify for the BC PTT exemption.

blocks.text: Why the window is open right now

parts.t: Three numbers from the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's August 2026 report:
, 33% above the ten-year average. More choice than any August in recent memory.
Anything under 12% is a buyer's market. Sellers are negotiating on price and accepting subject-to-financing offers again.
and roughly 15% below three years ago.

Put those together: the typical condo is under the zero-PTT line, there's more of them for sale than usual, and first-time buyers are still mostly on the sidelines. Less competition for the units that qualify for the full exemption.

Price isn't what stops most first-time buyers in the Fraser Valley. Qualification is. Every federally regulated lender qualifies you at your contract rate plus 2%, or 5.25%, whichever is higher. At today's rates that's roughly 6.4%, and it cuts your maximum purchase price by 15–20% versus what the payment calculator on a bank's website suggests.

A household earning $100,000 with no other debt qualifies for roughly $458,000 on a condo. That's under the benchmark. Two incomes, a 30-year amortization (now available to first-time buyers on insured mortgages), or paying down a car loan can each move that number meaningfully.
Know that number before you look at a single listing. It's the difference between a clean offer and a rejected one.

Jared Gibbons, Personal Real Estate Corporation · Royal LePage Little Oak Realty. Raised on a 40-acre farm in Langley, selling in the Fraser Valley for 11+ years.
